items.name: Saluting Device
items.blurb: A hat that tips itself when a person bows. U.S. patent 556,248, James C. Boyle, 1896.
items.docLine: Doc bows at the brim and the hat answers. He calls that manners with gears.
items.oogerLine: Ooger mutters, "hooo-mans cannot even lift their own hats."

items.name: Combined Plow and Gun
items.inventor: C. M. French and W. H. Fancher
items.blurb: A plow with a gun barrel built into the beam. U.S. patent 35,600, C. M. French and W. H. Fancher, 1862. It stays on the shelf as a story, not a product.
items.docLine: Doc will talk about the beam all day. He will not sell the plow.
items.oogerLine: Ooger pats the share. "hooo-mans mixed a field tool with a weapon. The shelf can keep it."

items.name: Storm-Mask
items.blurb: A wedge-nosed papier-mache storm mask. U.S. patent 587,687, Ulrich Harder, 1897. The shelf copy is a display replica, not something to wear.
items.docLine: Doc likes the nose. He says it parts the wind like a rude little boat.
items.oogerLine: Ooger squints. "hooo-mans hid from weather inside paper. Bold."

items.name: Quantum Lighter
items.blurb: A made-up lighter that is said to light one candle in three timelines at once. The case is sealed. There is no flame.
items.docLine: Doc taps the seal. One flame, three stories. He will not say which story is this one.
items.oogerLine: Ooger shrugs. "hooo-mans wanted a lighter that argues with itself."

items.name: Mustache-Guard
items.blurb: A small guard clipped to a spoon so soup misses a mustache. U.S. patent 411,988, May Evans Harrington, 1889.
items.docLine: Doc calls it a polite fence for soup.
items.oogerLine: Ooger grins with one tooth. "hooo-mans built a gate for a mustache."

items.name: Dimple Maker
items.blurb: A hand-cranked pair of arms meant to press a dimple into a cheek. U.S. patent 560,351, Martin Goetze, 1896. The shelf copy is for looking, not for cranking on anyone.
items.docLine: Doc will not demonstrate it on a visitor. He says the drawing is enough.
items.oogerLine: Ooger covers a cheek. "hooo-mans tried to crank a smile. That tracks."

items.name: Eye-Protector for Chickens
items.blurb: Tiny frames so a hen's neighbors cannot peck her eyes. U.S. patent 730,918, Andrew Jackson Jr., 1903.
items.docLine: Doc holds them up like small goggles and nods at hens who are not here.
items.oogerLine: Ooger blinks his big eyes. "Even birds needed a shield from the other birds."

items.name: Rocking Bath-Tub
items.blurb: A tub on rockers that was meant to slosh water at the person inside. U.S. patent 643,094, Otto A. Hensel, 1900. The shelf copy does not slosh, and it is not a treatment. Doc is not a doctor.
items.docLine: Doc rocks an empty model and looks pleased. He is not a doctor, and this is not a treatment.
items.oogerLine: Ooger steps back. "hooo-mans put a boat in the washroom."

items.name: Desk Plasma Globe
items.blurb: A glass ball of slow lightning for a desk. The warehouse does not make this one.
items.docLine: Doc stares into the glow and forgets the sentence he started.
items.oogerLine: Ooger taps the glass. "Pretty. Also not ours, hooo-mans."

items.name: Newton's Cradle
items.blurb: A row of metal balls that knock the next idea down the line. Sold by another shop.
items.docLine: Doc says the end ball knows what the first ball meant.
items.oogerLine: Ooger watches one click. "hooo-mans invented a polite argument."

items.name: Rube Goldberg Kit
items.blurb: A box of ramps, tracks, and little mishaps that end in one small result. Another shop sells it.
items.docLine: Doc wants twelve extra steps between the lever and the bell.
items.oogerLine: Ooger sighs. "hooo-mans never take the short hallway."

items.name: Jacob's Ladder Toy
items.blurb: Wooden blocks on ribbons that flip down as if they are walking. Another shop sells it.
items.docLine: Doc flips it once and calls the fall a staircase with commitment issues.
items.oogerLine: Ooger lets it clack. "It walks better than some hooo-mans."

items.name: Vintage Telegraph Key
items.blurb: A brass clicker from the age of dots and dashes. Another shop sells the old hardware.
items.docLine: Doc taps a hello he will not translate.
items.oogerLine: Ooger covers an ear. "hooo-mans used to shout with one finger."

items.name: Brass Kaleidoscope
items.blurb: A tube of mirrors that turns scraps into a fake stained-glass window. Another shop sells it.
items.docLine: Doc looks in, hums, and says the warehouse is the same trick at a larger size.
items.oogerLine: Ooger squints through it. "hooo-mans will stare at trash if it spins."

items.name: Model Stirling Engine
items.blurb: A little heat engine that spins when one side is warm and the other is not. Another shop sells the model.
items.docLine: Doc warms one palm near it and calls that a complete power plant.
items.oogerLine: Ooger nods. "It runs on a cup of tea. Ambitious for a desk model, hooo-mans."

items.name: Magic Lantern
items.blurb: An old picture projector that throws a painted slide on the wall. Another shop sells the lantern.
items.docLine: Doc treats every slide like a classified experiment.
items.oogerLine: Ooger shrugs. "hooo-mans have always wanted a bigger ghost on the wall."
